title: fleet-runway-matrix-order-staging
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet proposes a compact, operationally-light approach to smoothing accelerator fleet arrivals across regions while preserving SKU diversity and minimizing exposure to long lead-time skews. Focus is on: (a) converting bulk orders into micro-tranches, (b) maintaining a lightweight cross-region buffer lane, and (c) a simple runway calculation tied to measured per-region utilization.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Current inventory signals show concentrated arrivals in West-1 and East-2 for Q1-Q2. Lead-time variability from vendors (12–28 wks) is amplifying week-to-week burn volatility. Proposal: adopt a staggered order staging matrix where larger POs are split into 3–6 micro-tranches with randomized arrival offsets and explicit buffer lanes per region. This reduces peak arrival clustering, enables incremental testing of new SKUs, and yields a smoother usable-capacity curve for scheduling workloads.

Quick definitions (for this sheet):
- SKU = physical accelerator model (NVIDIA A100-80GB, H100-80GB, etc.)
- Micro-tranche = 5–25 units from a larger commitment, scheduled across multiple shipping windows
- Buffer lane = reserved inventory pool (hot/cold) allocated per region to absorb shortfalls and spikes
- Runway (weeks) = (inventory + committed_arrivals - 2*target_safety_stock) / burn_per_week

Current snapshot (as-of 2025-02-12):
Region statuses and rough counts (usable units):
- West-1: inventory 1,360 | committed arrivals 480 (next 12w) | avg burn 620/wk | runway = 3.5 wks
- East-2: inventory 980 | committed arrivals 1,120 (next 12w) | avg burn 410/wk | runway = 6.0 wks
- Central-3: inventory 420 | committed arrivals 160 (next 12w) | avg burn 140/wk | runway = 4.0 wks
- EU-West: inventory 300 | committed arrivals 200 (next 12w) | avg burn 210/wk | runway = 2.9 wks

SKU mix (high-level target vs current):
- H100-80GB: target 40% of fleet | current 34% | reason: preferred for high-throughput customers
- A100-80GB: target 30% | current 36% | reason: legacy slow-turnover SKUs increasing short-term availability
- LLM-optimized entry SKUs (L40x etc.): target 20% | current 18%
- Misc older/spot SKUs: target 10% | current 12%

Procurement pipeline ledger (sample, next 12 weeks view):
Columns: OrderID | SKU | Qty | Vendor ETA (weeks) | Tranche # | Region target | Status
- ORD-2025-1101 | H100-80GB | 300 | 18-22 | tranche 1/4 | West-1 | on-order
- ORD-2025-1101 | H100-80GB | 300 | 20-24 | tranche 2/4 | East-2 | on-order
- ORD-2025-1108 | A100-80GB | 150 | 8-12 | tranche 1/3 | Central-3 | confirmed
- ORD-2025-1115 | H100-80GB | 100 | 12-16 | tranche 3/4 | buffer-lane (EU-West) | pending-shipment
- ORD-2025-1120 | Mixed | 60 | 6-10 | single | East-2 | inbound-wk+7

Lead time smoothing strategy: micro-tranche ruleset (operational):
1) When creating a new PO > 100 units, split into 3 tranches by default: 50%, 30%, 20% (changeable for vendor constraints).
2) Assign each tranche a preferred region and a backup region. If a tranche ETA slips beyond threshold (+4 weeks), auto-reassign to backup and attempt cross-region swap.
3) Apply a randomized offset window of +/- 7 days on estimated ship dates for internal scheduling to avoid synchronized rack onboarding chores.
4) Reserve 15% of tranche qty as "test units" for validation on arrival; these are quarantined from immediate customer workload for 48–72h.

Safety-stock heuristic (simple):
- target_safety_stock = ceil( max(2, 0.25 * weekly_peak_burn) ) per region, floored at 20 units.
- Rationale: keeps small hot-pools for burst while not over-provisioning for low-utilization regions.

Runway table (example calculation for West-1):
- inventory 1360 + committed_arrivals 480 = 1840 usable next-12w
- weekly burn 620 -> 1840/620 = 2.97 wks raw. After safety-stock adjustment (2*SS where SS = 50): runway = (1840 - 100)/620 = 2.9 wks -> round to 3 wks. Note: apply smoothing using committed arrival tapering to show effective 6–8wk tail when staggered tranches arrive.

Cross-region buffer lane policy:
- Maintain a 5–8% fleet-wide buffer pool (cold) distributed proportionally by 7-day rolling usage.
- Hot buffer per region = max( floor(0.04 * region_capacity), 12 ) units kept for <24h burst.
- Cold buffer = redistribution candidates; usable after redeploy workflow (3–5 days).

Risk matrix (top-of-mind):
- Single-vendor concentration on H100 -> medium-high risk. Mitigation: diversify vendor roster; hold 2 micro-tranches per PO on alternative vendors when possible.
- Long-lead SKU mismatch -> risk: availability skew. Mitigation: increase micro-tranche count and schedule early tranches for validation.
- Customs/regional import delays -> risk: timing variance. Mitigation: allocate buffer-lane units in a nearby region as swap candidates.

Operational checklist (immediate next steps):
- [ ] Convert ORD-2025-1101 into 4 tranches in procurement system (owner: Arjun) -- due 2025-02-16
- [ ] Create cross-region swap playbook doc with SRE (owner: Priya) -- due 2025-02-20
- [ ] Update inventory dashboard to show tranche-level ETAs and per-region buffer counts (owner: Sofia) -- due 2025-02-18
- [ ] Run a dry-run redeploy of 12 cold-buffer units from West-1 -> EU-West to validate transfer latency (owner: Liam) -- target 2025-02-22

Metrics to track (weekly):
- Arrival variance (std dev of arrival per week) goal: reduce by 30% in 12 weeks
- Peak-deploy backlog (hrs) goal: reduce mean by 25%
- Cross-region swap success rate target: >85% within 7 days
- SKU diversity index (Herfindahl-like) target: keep below 0.35

Notes and open questions:
- Need legal review on tranche-based payment terms (some vendors require full payment on bulk POs).
- Confirm customs broker capacity in East-2 for increased tranche churn.
- Validate whether long-term commitments change pricing materially when orders are split; procurement to negotiate tranche-friendly terms.

Appendix: short sample weekly pipeline snapshot (text table)
Week | Expected arrivals (units) | Key SKUs | Notes
W+2  |  60  | Mixed (A100) | small inbound batch from ORD-2025-1120
W+5  | 120  | H100 tranche 1 | tentative West-1
W+8  | 150  | A100/H100 mixed | staggered tranche arrivals
W+12 | 200 | H100 tranche 2/3 | larger shipping window, monitor customs

If this approach looks reasonable we should run a pilot converting two outstanding large POs (ORD-2025-1101 and ORD-2025-1130) to the micro-tranche model and measure arrival variance and rack-onboarding backlog over a 12-week period.

Document history:
- 2024-11-07 initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2024-11-21 added tranche ruleset and buffer policy (Arjun P.)
- 2025-02-12 updated snapshot and operational checklist (Maya C.)

End of sheet.
